findings: The candidate preserves the only source-required constraints: exactly three sorted arrays and O(1) auxiliary space; it does not invent a stronger time-complexity requirement.

The conventional even-length median rule, int-array API, empty-input handling and no-mutation behavior are explicitly labelled as candidate implementation contracts rather than recovered source facts.
The three-pointer invariant is sufficient to justify that each selected value is the next value in the conceptual three-way merge, so stopping at the right-middle rank is correct.
The implementation allocates no input-sized structure and therefore satisfies O(1) auxiliary space; the test-only combined array is correctly separated from the production algorithm.
The long-before-average expression prevents overflow when the two central int values are both near either integer extreme.
Ten fixed cases plus 5000 deterministic randomized cases compare against a structurally different combined-sort oracle and also verify input immutability.
The follow-ups are question-specific and cover the core proof, space bound, even-length boundary, possible alternative complexity goals and empty-input contract.
No project history, size limit, online-judge attribution or unstated source constraint is fabricated. Human approval remains a separate promotion gate.
